highLevelGoal: Make Orca crash-safe at its core unattended-execution boundaries: durable repository actor/process ownership across controller death, no second writer under live/unknown prior ownership, atomic/replayable dispatch-control-completion transitions, and bounded initialization/profile cleanup.
activeChange: 028-durable-execution-ownership-and-crash-consistency (post-M24 focused hardening; Changes 026/027 remain open only for their residual external acceptance)

checkpoint.summary: 2026-08-26 next-campaign planner audit of pushed main 4d1246a: recursively inventoried the tracked repository and deeply reviewed the repository instructions/state/OpenSpec/CI plus controller lifecycle, SQLite stores/migrations, watcher, loop, executor, strategy/SWARM/DAG, worktree, scheduler, browser/profile and recovery boundaries. Selected focused Change 028 after confirming no open issue/PR supersedes it. Critical finding F1: restart reconciliation declares pending/running executor/worker processes gone without durable PID/process identity; RECOVERY_REQUIRED is outside active ownership, so a surviving old child can coexist with a newly-started writer. Critical finding F2: dispatch/control/completion source consumption and required run transitions are split durable writes; a crash can leave consumed-but-unapplied protocol truth with no watcher replay. High findings: fire-and-forget critical callbacks, startup/listen teardown that can bypass resources created during buildApp rehydrate, and automated profile stale ownership tied to controller PID rather than surviving Chrome. Planning artifacts only; no runtime implementation was performed in this planner commit.
